title: Lunceford's finances, Hammond and the move back to Basie
summary: When the band's corporation ended and pay was cut, John Hammond told him Basie needed arrangements, and Basie offered $75 for playing and $75 for arranging.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: It must have been '38. I stayed with him four years, didn't I?
Well, I was wondering, you got $65 then?

He gave me $35 when I first started. But (unintelligible) when on and made $4,000 or $5,000 in one night. And so they had a corporation, and when he went to Larchmont from that air. He went on the air and then he said, there ain't no more corporation.
Oh, that was when the corporation --
It was all the cut rate, and the guys said, man, we ain't going to get cut and he said, we can't handle it no more. Ain't got it no more. (Unintelligible.)
That's when it started to break up then.

Yeah. Then, they played a date and John Hammond came out and saw me and I said, well, -- he said, Basie's short. I said, well, I promised to come back for a year. And Basie running short, he said, they only got
12 numbers and your arrangements in the Roseland, they need more stuff like that. And they ain't got nobody to write it. I said, well, I told you (unintelligible). I say, I'll come over.
So I gave Lunceford notice. And they gave me $75 for playing and $75 for arranging. I went into the big money.
That was a big step up.
